title: Sunny and the Cockatoo Family | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka discovers a whole family of sulphur-crested cockatoos roosting together in a moonlit gum tree, all pressed in close, crest feathers folded flat, completely at peace. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The gum tree held a family.

Sunny saw them before she heard them — which was unusual for cockatoos. In the daytime they were the loudest birds in the bush, squawking and wheeling and demanding to be noticed. But now, in the deep of the night, there was nothing. Just shapes in the branches.

She counted seven of them.

They were pressed together in pairs and clusters on three branches — white shapes in the dark, their yellow crests folded flat against their heads. No squawking. No dramatics. Just seven large white birds, completely still, completely quiet.

She had never seen cockatoos like this.

She had only ever seen them being loud.

She sat down under the tree and looked up.

One of them shifted on its branch — a small adjustment, a lifting and re-settling of its feet — and for a moment its crest lifted slightly, yellow in the moonlight, then folded flat again. Then it was still.

All that loud, she thought. All that noise and colour and commotion — and underneath it, they just needed each other. They needed to be together on a branch in the dark.

She leaned against the tree.

The family slept, pressed close.

She thought about her own small, close, quiet things.

And slept.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, cockatoo family. Goodnight, little one.
